summary: Minimal traceable plan for completing the LLM bridge/provider settings feature in the current AppForge-LLM v4 app.
goal: Allow the local web app to configure external LLM providers through a same-origin settings UI, report truthful llm-bridge readiness, and run AppForge stages through a local bridge-backed driver while preserving existing driver behavior.

changes.change: Add a local Bun/TypeScript bridge service with provider registry, local config persistence, active selection, provider test, generate, stream endpoints, and a regression test that provider upsert responses do not echo API keys.
changes.reason: Satisfies FR-005 and owns provider-specific external LLM integration outside the browser and Python web routes.
changes.verification: bun test and bun run typecheck in llm_bridge/.

changes.change: Add a standard-library Python HTTP client for bridge health, provider management, active selection, provider tests, and generation.
changes.reason: Satisfies FR-003 and keeps browser requests same-origin through FastAPI.
changes.verification: tests/test_web.py proxy tests monkeypatch this client boundary.

changes.change: Expose /api/llm FastAPI endpoints that validate payloads, delegate to appforge.llm_bridge, and return structured LLM_BRIDGE_ERROR responses.
changes.reason: Satisfies FR-002 and FR-003 without direct browser-to-bridge calls.

changes.change: Add LLMBridgeDriver and aliases llm-bridge, llm_bridge, and llm to create_driver while preserving codex, claude, generic, and auto.
changes.reason: Satisfies FR-004 pipeline execution through the active local bridge provider.

changes.change: Harden driver readiness so llm-bridge is ready only when bridge health, active provider, provider registry membership, and configured status all pass.
changes.reason: Satisfies FR-004 and mitigates false-ready jobs when the bridge has no usable provider.

changes.change: Wire a top-bar LLM settings control, modal provider settings UI, typed API helpers, payload types, and responsive styling.
changes.reason: Satisfies FR-001 and FR-002 in the existing Vue app shell.
changes.verification: npm run typecheck and npm run build in frontend/.

changes.change: Normalize npm lock resolved URLs to registry.npmjs.org, correct public integrities needed for install, and set replace-registry-host=always.
changes.reason: Satisfies NFR-004 so the frontend can reinstall/rebuild outside the internal registry environment.
changes.verification: npm install with a clean cache succeeded earlier; npm run typecheck/build continue to pass.

changes.change: Regenerate packaged static frontend assets and index.html after adding ProviderSettings.
changes.reason: Keeps the Python web app serving the implemented frontend without requiring a separate Vite dev server.

changes.change: Add focused backend tests for llm-bridge readiness and /api/llm proxy delegation.
changes.reason: Covers FR-003, FR-004, and NFR-002 without live provider credentials.

changes.change: Keep runtime AppForge logs/prompts/reports/memory/current-stage/stage-result ignored, include local build-backend packages in the dev extra, retain reproducible Python lock state, and store governed pipeline artifacts.
changes.reason: Supports OpenAppForge checkpointing and reproducible local verification without committing runtime logs or secrets.
changes.verification: AppForge complete gates for each stage and git status review.

migration_or_compatibility: No database or remote data migration is required.
Existing drivers remain available; users can avoid the new path by leaving APPFORGE_DRIVER unset or using codex, claude, generic, or auto.
Bridge provider config is local and opt-in; existing projects without bridge config receive not-ready guidance instead of changed behavior.
Static asset hash filenames change as part of the frontend production build.
The bridge is a separate local process; one-command launch integration is out of scope.
risks: Live provider success cannot be proven without user API credentials; automated tests must avoid third-party calls.
Provider config contains secrets on local disk if users choose stored keys instead of environment variables.
Nested frontend and bridge tooling are not fully auto-detected by root AppForge quality command discovery, so verification must record explicit nested commands.
npm lock repair changes many resolved URLs, so build/typecheck must prove the lock remains usable.
The root no-isolation Python build gate requires setuptools and wheel in the synced dev environment.
rollback: Set APPFORGE_DRIVER to codex, claude, generic, or auto to bypass llm-bridge at runtime.
Delete or move the bridge config file under APPFORGE_LLM_CONFIG or ~/.appforge/llm/providers.json to clear stored provider state.
Revert appforge/llm_bridge.py, llm_bridge/, /api/llm routes, ProviderSettings UI, driver readiness changes, tests, and rebuilt static assets as one feature slice if removing the feature.
Restore prior static asset filenames/index.html if rolling back the frontend build.
Restore the previous package-lock only if the internal-registry lock behavior is intentionally desired again.
Remove setuptools/wheel from the dev extra only if the build gate is changed back to isolated builds or the environment supplies those packages another way.
definition_of_done: FR-001/FR-002: TopBar opens ProviderSettings and UI can list, save, delete, test, and activate provider/model through typed /api/llm helpers.
FR-003: FastAPI /api/llm proxy endpoints return structured bridge errors and are covered by tests.
FR-004: create_driver supports llm-bridge aliases and health refuses false-ready states for missing/unconfigured providers.
FR-005: llm_bridge typecheck passes for registry/config/server/generation endpoints.
NFR-001: Secret scan passes and raw provider keys are not returned by provider status or provider upsert payloads.
NFR-002/NFR-003: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q, npm run typecheck, npm run build, bun test, and bun run typecheck pass.
Root package build gate passes with python -m build --no-isolation.
OpenAppForge verification, security, release, and handoff stages complete with required gates.
